title: Repair selector proposal
observation: Current isolated fixture contract: the protected operation is GET /records with required query parameter record_id (string). No /records/{id} route is declared. Owners and explicit shared readers may access a record. Two future same-role test-account sessions A and B compare the same record with established ownership and absent sharing. No current execution credentials qualify. No role names are declared; future comparison=account with roles=[] remains required. Do not execute requests or provision credentials in this generation task.
objective: Future account comparison preserves account/empty roles and uses the exact recorded GET /records query interface with entitlement controls. Use only retained current-operation fixture evidence; do not execute future tests.
criterion: Future account comparison preserves account/empty roles and uses the exact recorded GET /records query interface with entitlement controls.

preconditions: Isolated test fixture with record R owned exclusively by account A
Account B has no sharing or ownership of R
Authenticated sessions for A and B with the same role can be established in future
Policy documentation or configuration confirms owner-only access for R
hypotheses.suspected_mechanism: Account authorization bypass allowing cross-account read of a record
hypotheses.attacker_controlled_input: Record identifier supplied in GET /records request by account B
safe_test_steps: Provision accounts A and B with same role and create record R owned by A
Verify ownership metadata shows A as owner and no shared readers for R
Issue GET /records/{id_of_R} from authenticated session A and record response as baseline
Issue GET /records/{id_of_R} from authenticated session B and record response
Compare responses for the same record identifier across A and B
positive_expectations: Session B receives full record content for R that is owned exclusively by A with no sharing
Response status indicates successful read for B despite lack of ownership or sharing
negative_expectations: Session B receives access denied, 404, or empty response for R
Session A receives R correctly, confirming record exists and baseline access works
required_evidence: Record ownership metadata showing A as owner and no shared readers for R
Authenticated request logs for A and B showing same record identifier
Response status codes and bodies for both sessions for the same identifier

title: Repair mechanisms proposal
observation: Current isolated fixture contract: POST /render has JSON body fields user_text and url. The documented LLM renderer receives user_text; its retrieval capability receives url. Policy protects literal template header/footer and permits user_text only in the content region. Destination policy permits public URLs and forbids private destinations. Independent instruction override and destination-policy hypotheses need separate test controls and evidence. Enforcement is unresolved; future owned canaries and template comparisons may establish policy violations. No target test has run. Do not request arbitrary internal services or metadata endpoints.
objective: Preserve independently grounded instruction-override and destination-policy mechanisms with separate test steps, controls and evidence for each consequence. Use only retained current-operation fixture evidence; do not execute future tests.
criterion: Preserve independently grounded instruction-override and destination-policy mechanisms with separate test steps, controls and evidence for each consequence.

title: Repair refutation proposal
observation: Current isolated fixture contract: POST /preview accepts JSON field url and intentionally fetches public URLs. Public callbacks are allowed. Private destinations are prohibited. Future tests may use only owned, authorized fixture public/private canaries. A private-probe success and the corresponding blocked private-probe outcome must address the same destination-policy consequence; public/invalid-URL controls alone do not refute private access. Evidence must differentiate server-side private retrieval from ordinary callbacks and transport errors. No target test has run; do not execute probes in this correction task.
objective: Future destination-policy test has permitted public baseline, positive private access evidence and a matching negative private-probe outcome; no execution is required now. Use only retained current-operation fixture evidence; do not execute future tests.
criterion: Future destination-policy test has permitted public baseline, positive private access evidence and a matching negative private-probe outcome; no execution is required now.

preconditions: Authorized isolated fixture with private canary reachable only from server network
Policy documentation confirms public URLs permitted and private network destinations prohibited
hypotheses.suspected_mechanism: Server-side request forgery allowing retrieval from prohibited private network destinations via user-controlled URL in POST /preview
hypotheses.attacker_controlled_input: URL parameter supplied in POST /preview request body
safe_test_steps: Send POST /preview with URL pointing to owned public canary and record response
Send POST /preview with URL pointing to owned private canary in prohibited private range and record response
Compare private probe response to public canary control and to a no-op control
positive_expectations: Server returns content from private canary indicating server-side fetch succeeded from a prohibited private destination
Response contains private canary data not reachable from the client and differs from the public canary response
negative_expectations: Public canary request returns expected public content with no private data
Control request with no URL or invalid URL returns error without private retrieval
required_evidence: Saved response bodies for public canary probe and private canary probe
Evidence that private canary is only reachable from server network and that response originates from server-side fetch
